_comment: Configuration for the SHP -> DIgSILENT DGS converter. Edit mappings/factors as needed.

transformer._comment_series: Loss-class ('series') selection: AB' = low-loss, Normal = standard. Scanned fields are checked for the keyword lists below; low-loss keywords win if both appear. Per user instruction, low-loss (AB') is also the default when nothing is mentioned.
transformer._comment_insulation: Insulation ('O'=oil, 'D'=dry) selection from insulation_field, matched against the keyword lists below.
transformer._comment_patterns: Ordered candidate loc_name patterns tried per insulation, first exact match wins. {series}/{cap} are substituted; falls back to type_pattern/capacity-based matching if none match.

fuse._comment: Fuse types are selected from the rated current carried by the source data (current_field), matched against the TypFuse rows of the type library (types_override.xlsx: Fuse_Type_1 ... Fuse_Type_100, urat 20 kV). type_name_pattern is tried first; then an exact irat match; then the nearest available rating (snap_prefer: lower = never over-rate a device).
fuse._comment_unknown: Fuses whose rated current is 0 / empty / unparsable are far too numerous to review by hand, so the rating is derived instead: take the capacity of the nearest MV transformer (in practice the fuse on that transformer's MV busbar) and read the rating from capacity_current_table. The MV (20 kV) fuse type for that rating is then used, exactly as if the data had carried it. only if no transformer is within capacity_max_distance_m does type_name apply.
fuse._comment_distance: Maximum distance (in the shapefiles' own map units, normally metres) between a fuse and the transformer whose capacity it may borrow; 0 disables the limit. Raise it if your exports digitise the cutout several tens of metres from the transformer symbol.

_comment_layers: Shapefile layer-name defaults per the utility's official layer list (see 'attachments'). lv_fuse/lv_switch/lv_distribution_box have no corresponding entry in that list, so their prior codes were kept rather than guessed -- override per-project via the Layer Mapping settings if your data differs from any of these.

graphics._comment: v2.3 diagram sizes, in DIgSILENT diagram units. node_spacing/terminal_size/busbar_length/busbar_thickness/element_size are FIXED values (not scaled by the network's real-world extent) so symbols stay a sensible, predictable size regardless of feeder length. Only page_margin_ratio/page_margin_min scale with the data's real extent, to keep a sensible gap between the outermost elements and the page edge.

line_type._comment_covered: Covered-conductor ('CC') names follow the base conductor in the shipped type library: MINK=70, HYENA=126, WOLF=185 mm2. Sections with no covered entry (e.g. 225/226/LYNX) fall back to covered_default and are listed in the discrepancy report.
line_type._comment_underground: NA2XSY/N2XSY XLPE underground-cable naming (VDE convention: NA = aluminum conductor, N = copper conductor, 2X = XLPE insulation, S = copper-wire screen, Y = PVC sheath). Invalid/unrecognised section or material falls back to uml_default and is recorded in the discrepancy report and prescan.

capacitor._comment: No reactive-power rating field was identified in the source shapefile schema for capacitor banks, so a configurable default is used for every capacitor point -- review per-unit values in the Type Library Editor or override individually if your data has a rating field.

lv_line_type._comment: LV (0.4kV) line/cable types are NOT present in the original MV-only dgs_template.json, so GeoGrid synthesizes them at conversion time from these rules, one TypLne row per distinct (material, section, installation) combination actually found in the input data. rline is computed from standard conductor resistivity (physics-based, reliable). xline/Ithr use single typical per-category values (textbook approximations) since exact manufacturer catalogue data was not available -- review/replace the generated LV types in the Type Library Editor (or via types_override) before using results for real engineering decisions.
